explain.say: Around 750, Chang'an, the Tang capital, may have been the largest city on Earth, with perhaps a million people. Persian merchants, Sogdian dancers, Japanese students and Buddhist monks walked its grid of streets. Look at the timeline: six and a half centuries from Tang glory to Song invention.

explain.say: Look at the map. Sogdian traders from Samarkand came east to Chang'an, and Japan copied its plan for a new capital at Nara in 710. Chang'an was the centre of a whole world of East Asian culture. Why would a neighbouring kingdom copy another's capital?

Then, in 755, a general named An Lushan rebelled. See the sizes: the census fell from about 52.9 million people in 754 to 16.9 million in 764. Many died, but historians think much of the drop shows the state losing track of people. What does that teach you about reading old numbers?

draw.text: A census counts who the state can reach.

explain.say: Now the inventions. The Diamond Sutra of 868 is the oldest dated printed book. Under the Song came government paper money in 1024, the first gunpowder formulas in 1044, and compasses used at sea. Faster-ripening rice fed a population of perhaps 100 million. Which of these still shapes your daily life?

explain.say: The Japanese historian Naito Konan called the change from Tang to Song a transition to an early modern China, and Mark Elvin spoke of a medieval economic revolution. The Song finally fell to the Mongols in 1279. Brilliant work. Exam tip: link each invention to trade, cities and the exam-trained official class.

faq.q: What did the Song dynasty invent?
faq.a: The Song saw government paper money from 1024, the first written gunpowder formulas in 1044, movable type described in the 1040s, the magnetic compass used at sea, and big advances in shipbuilding, iron production and rice farming.

faq.q: Why was the An Lushan rebellion important?
faq.a: The rebellion of 755 to 763 devastated north China, weakened central control for the rest of the Tang and shifted power to regional governors. The census fell from about 53 to 17 million, partly from deaths and partly from collapsed registration.
A Buddhist text printed with woodblocks and dated to 868. Found in a cave at Dunhuang, it is the oldest surviving dated printed book and is now in the British Library.
asks: What is the oldest printed book?

faq.q: When was paper money first used?
faq.a: Merchants in Sichuan used private notes called jiaozi in the early eleventh century, and the Song government took over issuing them in 1024, making the first state paper money.

The idea, first argued by Naito Konan, that between the eighth and twelfth centuries China changed from an aristocratic society to one run by exam-selected officials, with booming markets, cities and technology.

facts: The Tang dynasty ruled from 618 to 907 and the Song from 960 to 1279.
The Diamond Sutra, dated 868, is the oldest surviving dated printed book.
The Song government issued paper money from 1024.
